pick.headline: US Ambassador Dubs killed in Kabul
pick.summary: On February 14, 1979, US Ambassador Adolph Dubs was kidnapped in Kabul and killed when Afghan security forces, advised by Soviet officials, stormed the hotel room where he was held.
pick.significance: Washington protested the handling of the rescue and cut aid to Afghanistan. The killing deepened the US-Soviet distrust that preceded the invasion that December.
pick.fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of February 14, 1979, carried Kabul radio's Urdu service account: "terrorists" in traffic-police dress seized Ambassador Dubs and held him at the Kabul Hotel, and he was shot when security forces acted; Taraki sent Carter a message of sorrow.

alternates.headline: Guerrillas briefly seize US Embassy in Tehran
alternates.summary: On February 14, 1979, leftist guerrillas stormed the US Embassy in Tehran and held its staff for several hours before forces loyal to Khomeini evicted them.
alternates.significance: The 'Valentine's Day open house' foreshadowed the far longer seizure of November 1979.
alternates.fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of February 14, 1979, carried Tehran Domestic Service: the revolution's provisional staff said "soldiers of the revolution" were guarding the U.S. Embassy, and, citing AP, that attackers had taken it over and held 70 Americans including Ambassador Sullivan.
